Transmission study · Embodied judgment → institutional memory

How a Fashion House Transfers Tacit Knowledge

A house transfers tacit knowledge by pairing records with situated practice: demonstration, attempt, correction, comparison, narration, and trusted authority. The goal is not to extract every secret, but to preserve what collaborators may ethically carry.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

A technical file can specify measurement and material while failing to explain the practiced hand that senses tension, recognizes a wrong drape, or chooses when an exception protects the design. The surviving Worth ensemble makes that limitation concrete: the object holds evidence of material and construction but cannot replay the conversations and corrections that formed it.

FIT’s Patternmaking Department oral history preserves practitioner voices; UNESCO’s textile-safeguarding work documents knowledge transmission in specific communities; the Ferré Research Center organizes archival material for research. These sources support multiple transmission mechanisms, not one formula for every house.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · SHOW

What must be demonstrated?

Identify judgments that resist prose: hand position, tension, sequence, sound, resistance, drape, finishing threshold, and the moment an expert stops. Record only with informed permission.

INFERENCES72S73S88

02 · TRY

Where does the learner practice?

Design a bounded attempt using sacrificial material, time for repetition, and permission to fail. Apprenticeship is labor and education; compensation, safety, access, and jurisdiction must be addressed.

PROPOSALS73S76S87

03 · CORRECT

How is judgment calibrated?

Preserve paired examples, expert commentary, acceptable variation, non-negotiable failure, and the reason for correction. Record disagreement instead of forcing false consensus.

PROPOSALS72S74S88

04 · RETURN

Who retains authority over the knowledge?

Define consent, attribution, confidentiality, access, benefit, revocation, cultural authority, archive custody, and successor permissions. Not all knowledge should become a company asset or public lesson.

PROPOSALS88S21S22

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Documentation can democratize access, but it can also extract knowledge from workers and communities, freeze evolving practice, expose trade secrets, or privilege what a camera can capture. Ethical transfer includes the right not to record and the power to govern future use.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Ask a practitioner to identify one decision a specification cannot teach.
  2. With consent, record demonstration, learner attempt, correction, acceptable variation, and stop condition.
  3. Attach contributor, compensation, confidentiality, cultural-authority, access, archive, and revocation terms.
  4. Have the practitioner and, where appropriate, a cultural specialist approve the description before publication.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical essay: The Knowledge Between Hand and Record
  • Demonstration–attempt–correction film treatment
  • Eight-frame tacit-transfer carousel
  • Four apprenticeship verticals
  • Tacit Knowledge Transfer Protocol
  • Newsletter, oral-history, workshop, and archive editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Film one permitted process in five layers: expert demonstration, learner attempt, correction, second attempt, practitioner-approved narration. Include a visible “not recorded by choice” field.

02

SHORT 01 — “A specification tells you what. Tacit knowledge often tells you when, how much, and why this exception.”

03

SHORT 02 — The ethical archive test: who consented, who was paid, who can access it, who may teach it, who can withdraw it?

04

CAROUSEL — Show; try; correct; compare; narrate; govern; return; continue. Every frame names a record and a human authority.

05

AUDIO — A practitioner oral-history script centered on decisions, sensory cues, disagreement, and boundaries—not extraction of proprietary technique.

06

WORKSHOP — Build one paired-example lesson, then submit its labor, confidentiality, cultural, accessibility, and archive terms for specialist review.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
